recipe.title: Hungarian Goulash with Chuck Tender Steak
recipe.description: A deep red paprika broth gone silky around fall-apart cubes of beef, sweet peppers and baby potatoes. Slow simmered on the stove, finished with red wine vinegar and parsley — a bowl you eat with a spoon and nothing else.

ingredients.item: Chuck Tender Steak (Hormel) (new buy), trimmed of visible fat and cut into 3 cm cubes
Onions, white, halved and thinly sliced
Tomatoes, raw, cored and roughly chopped
Baby potatoes (The Little Potato Co.), halved (quartered if larger than a walnut)
Red bell pepper (new buy), seeded and cut into 2 cm strips

steps.title: Season the raw beef
steps.content: Pat the raw beef cubes dry with paper towel — wet meat steams instead of browning. Season them all over with salt and pepper. Pro tip: dry surface plus a hot pan is where the whole colour of this stew comes from.

steps.title: Sear the beef in two batches
steps.content: Heat a heavy pot on the stove over high (8-9 of 10) with the olive oil, 20 g. Add half the beef in a single layer and leave it alone 2 minutes, then turn and give it 2 more, until deeply browned on two sides. Move it to a plate and sear the second half the same way. Don't crowd the pot — that's what makes it grey.

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.content: Drop the heat to medium (5 of 10). Add the sliced onions to the pot with a pinch of salt and cook 8 minutes, scraping the browned bits off the bottom as they release, until soft and golden at the edges.

steps.title: Bloom the paprika
steps.content: Pull the pot OFF the heat. Stir in the garlic, 12 g, the paprika, 2 tbsp, and the ground caraway, 1 tsp, and stir for about 30 seconds in the residual heat. Pro tip: paprika scorches and turns bitter in seconds over a live flame — off the heat is not optional here.

steps.title: Build the braise
steps.content: Return the pot to the stove over medium. Add the chopped tomatoes and the beef broth, 500 g, and scrape the bottom clean. Return the seared beef and any juices from the plate. Bring to a gentle simmer (3-4 of 10 — small bubbles, not a boil).

steps.title: Simmer the beef tender
steps.content: Cover and simmer at 3-4 for 75 minutes, stirring once or twice. The beef should be starting to give when pressed with a spoon.

steps.title: Add potatoes and peppers
steps.content: Stir in the halved potatoes and the pepper strips. Re-cover and simmer another 30 minutes, until the potatoes are fully tender and the beef pulls apart under a spoon.

steps.title: Thicken and finish
steps.content: Crush 3 or 4 potato halves against the side of the pot with the back of the spoon and stir — that starch is what turns the broth silky, no flour needed. Stir in the red wine vinegar, 10 g, then taste and correct the salt and pepper. Scatter the chopped parsley over the bowls at the table.

recipe.notes: Per serving: protein ~39 g | calories ~535 | saturated fat ~5 g | added sugar 0 g | fiber ~9 g. New buys: chuck tender steak, red bell pepper, beef broth, fresh parsley, ground caraway (the caraway jar is the signature flavour of real goulash and keeps for a year). Storage: better on day two — cool and refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat on Steam in the Tovala or on the stove at 3-4, adding a splash of water if it has tightened. Freezes well for 3 months. Pro tips: cut the beef into even 3 cm cubes so they finish together; if you want it hands-off, do steps 1-5 in the morning, then move everything to the slow cooker on LOW 6 hours, adding potatoes and peppers for the last 90 minutes. Fatty liver: this is the classic dish, not a diet version — goulash was never made with butter or cream, so it only needed lean chuck tender instead of fatty chuck roast, a measured 20 g of olive oil, and potatoes and peppers doing half the plate. Vinegar at the end does what wine would have.

recipe.title: Moroccan Lamb & Chickpea Stew
recipe.description: Lean lamb leg braised until it gives way, in a cumin-and-cinnamon tomato broth with sweet carrots and chickpeas. It reduces down thick enough to coat the spoon, then gets a fistful of fresh cilantro and a hard squeeze of lime right at the table. Serves 3.

ingredients.item: Boneless lamb leg, trimmed of all visible fat and cut into 2.5 cm cubes (new buy)
Carrots, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks (new buy)
Tomatoes, raw, cored and roughly chopped
Canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed (new buy)
Fresh cilantro, leaves and tender stems, roughly chopped (new buy)

steps.title: Season the raw lamb
steps.content: Pat the raw lamb cubes dry with paper towel and season them all over with salt and pepper. Dry meat is the whole difference between a sear and a steam.

steps.title: Sear the lamb in batches
steps.content: Heat 15 g of the olive oil in a heavy pot over high heat (8-9) until it shimmers. Sear the lamb in two batches, about 4 minutes per batch, turning the cubes once they release from the pot, until deeply browned on two sides. Don't crowd the pot. Move the seared lamb to a plate — it is still raw in the middle and finishes in the braise.

steps.title: Soften the onion and carrot
steps.content: Turn the heat down to medium (5) and add the remaining 10 g olive oil. Add the diced onion and the carrot chunks and cook 6-7 minutes, stirring and scraping up the browned bits from the bottom, until the onion is translucent and the pot is deglazed by the vegetable moisture.

steps.title: Bloom the spices and paste
steps.content: Add the minced garlic, cumin, cinnamon and paprika and stir for 45 seconds until fragrant. Add the tomato paste and cook it another 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens to a brick red — that's where the depth comes from.

steps.title: Build the braise
steps.content: Add the chopped tomatoes and the chicken broth, then return the lamb and any juices from the plate. Stir, bring to a boil over high heat, then drop to a simmer (3-4 on the dial — small bubbles, never a rolling boil). Cover and cook 90 minutes, stirring every 30 minutes, until the lamb is fork-tender.

steps.title: Add chickpeas and thicken
steps.content: Stir in the drained chickpeas. Uncover, raise to a strong simmer (4-5) and cook 15-20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the broth reduces and coats the back of a spoon. Crush a few chickpeas against the side of the pot with your spoon to thicken it further.

steps.title: Finish with cilantro and lime
steps.content: Off the heat, taste and adjust salt and pepper. Stir in half the chopped cilantro, scatter the rest over the top, and serve with the lime wedges to squeeze over each bowl. The acid at the end wakes the whole pot up — don't skip it.

recipe.notes: Per serving: ~43 g protein, ~570 calories, ~5 g saturated fat, 0 g added sugar, ~13 g fiber. New buys: lamb leg, carrots, tomato paste, chicken broth, canned chickpeas, fresh cilantro, ground cumin, ground cinnamon (the spices are long-life jars you'll use again). Everything else came from your shelf — onion, tomatoes, garlic, olive oil, paprika, lime. Storage: it's better on day two; keeps 4 days covered in the fridge and freezes well for 3 months. Reheat in the Tovala on Steam for 8-10 minutes so the lamb stays tender instead of drying out in the microwave. Pro tips: buy leg rather than shoulder and trim it hard — shoulder carries the fat that would blow the saturated fat budget. If you'd rather come home to it, do the sear and the spice/paste step on the stove, then move everything to the slow cooker on LOW for 6 hours and add the chickpeas for the last 30 minutes with the lid off. Fatty liver: this is the classic tagine minus the butter, the honey and the dried fruit — the sweetness comes from carrots and cooked-down onion instead, the fat is 25 g of measured olive oil, and the chickpeas carry the fiber so no bread or couscous is needed to make it a full dinner.
